# Fuigo release provenance

Murage pins Fuigo **1.0.13** as a separate native executable. The engine requires no global Node, npm or Fuigo installation inside a packaged app.

The [official npm manifest](https://registry.npmjs.org/fuigo/1.0.13) declares six exact-version platform dependencies. Each registry archive was downloaded and checked byte-identical to the matching `fuigo-<target>-1.0.13.tgz` in the `npm-packages-1.0.13` artifact of the upstream release workflow run that published it, and against the SHA-512 integrity and SHA-1 shasum values in both that artifact's `release-manifest.json` and the public npm metadata (whose `gitHead` is the same source commit). SHA-256 pins below were computed from those exact archives and their Brotli-decompressed executables, and each executable header was read to confirm its architecture (Mach-O arm64 / x86_64, ELF `0xb7` / `0x3e`, PE `0xaa64` / `0x8664`). No npm postinstall script was run to obtain the binaries.

Source: `1f5f89ab3aa994cfcaf8e0550942ce9cd42342d1` (tag `v1.0.13`, the merge of `release/1.0.13`; `release-manifest.json` `sourceCommit` and the npm `gitHead` of all seven packages name the same commit). Canonical archives: [release workflow run 34623419288](https://github.com/FerroxLabs/fuigo/actions/runs/34623419288), all jobs successful: the six per-target builds, "assemble and publish" (whose "Verify release archives" step passed) and the six "verify npm" jobs. **No GitHub release `v1.0.13` existed at bump time and none is expected**: the upstream release workflow publishes to npm only, as it did for 1.0.12. The workflow artifact carries no `SHA256SUMS`, so the SHA-256 values in the table were computed here over the artifact archives (byte-identical to the registry bytes) and are the reviewed digests. The darwin-arm64 executable was run on the build Mac and reports `fuigo 1.0.13 (1f5f89ab3aa9)`.

The existing `scripts/prepare-fuigo.mjs` validates both digests and the executable header before staging. Existing platform selection remains unchanged; this bump adds no platform or parser support. The 1.0.13 arm64 engines are still ELF aarch64 and PE ARM64, which the shared header parser does not classify, so linux-arm64 and win32-arm64 stay pinned but unstageable. Staged files remain in ignored `dist-native/fuigo/`. `MURAGE_FUIGO_ARCHIVE_DIR` can supply the reviewed archives without another download.

## License and memory

The Apache-2.0 LICENSE, NOTICE, comprehensive dependency notices and vendored notices are copied from the published package into this directory and packaged as `licenses/fuigo-*`. At 1.0.13 they are byte-identical to the copies already vendored here (unchanged since 1.0.11, re-compared at this bump), and identical across all six platform packages. Existing named license links remain available. Package checksums are not code-signing or notarization proof; application signing continues through its existing packaging process.

Fuigo enables local workspace memory by default (since 1.0.9). Global sharing, remote embeddings and automatic model consolidation remain opt-in. Murage explicitly passes `--no-memory` before `agent` and `--no-leader` for every hosted turn, so Murage remains the memory owner even when ambient `FUIGO_MEMORY=1` or standalone configuration enables Fuigo memory. The 1.0.13 executable still accepts that exact argument order. Standalone Fuigo configuration is not rewritten. This dependency update does not rewrite user configuration or migrate memory/session stores.

## Tool presentation (1.0.11)

Fuigo 1.0.11 added an opt-in `FUIGO_TOOL_PRESENTATION` setting. The default, `full`, sends the same tool set as 1.0.10. `compact` shortens descriptions for 13 built-in tools; `adaptive` also holds back native media-generation schemas until `search_tool` with `scope: "native"` discovers them. Tool names, parameter schemas, permissions, hooks and AGENTS.md handling are unchanged in every mode, and discovery never grants permission. Murage does not set this variable. Like other ambient `FUIGO_*` settings it reaches the hosted engine unchanged, so a user who opts in outside Murage gets the same presentation inside Murage. Provider credential routing and permission prompts retain the existing Murage driver behavior.

## Headless sessions and `ask_user_question` (1.0.12)

Fuigo 1.0.12 stops advertising `ask_user_question` to non-interactive sessions (`fuigo -p`, SDK), because nobody is there to answer. The gate is: an explicit `_meta.askUserQuestion` on `session/new` wins; otherwise `_meta.startupHints.nonInteractive` turns the tool off; otherwise the `ask_user_question` feature decides. Murage's ACP driver sends neither key, so its sessions resolve as interactive and the tool is advertised exactly as under 1.0.11; the `_fuigo/ask_user_question` request shape and the answer path Murage renders as a question card are unchanged. The rest of 1.0.12 is engine-side (OpenAI models default to the Codex harness, opt-in OpenAI Responses programmatic tool calling, whole-file and multi-path `read_file` with a read-dedupe cache, synchronous-by-default `spawn_subagent`, tool-list stability across side calls) and needs no Murage driver change.

## Folder trust and permission tightening (1.0.13)

Fuigo 1.0.13 is a security and reliability release with no protocol change, but it is the first published build in which the folder-trust gate is actually live. Upstream commit `3b8664ae` found that the release workflow never stamped `FUIGO_VERSION`, so every published 1.0.11 and 1.0.12 binary identified as a dev build and `folder_trust_inert()` auto-trusted every folder: repo-local MCP/LSP servers, hooks, plugins and permission rules loaded ungated. 1.0.13 stamps the version, and its `project_scope_allowed` gate now also covers project instructions (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, rules directories) and project skills/commands (`.fuigo/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.cursor/`). ACP sessions consult the gate at session setup and on skill refresh. It never blocks: a trust prompt is only offered when stdin and stderr are both terminals or the client advertised `fuigo/folderTrust.interactive`, and Murage's piped `agent stdio` spawn is neither, so before 0.1.52's FUIGOTRUST1 an untrusted folder that shipped any of those sources resolved fail-closed and the turn silently ran without them. Sources under `~/.fuigo/` always load; a folder the user has trusted in standalone Fuigo (`fuigo --trust`, persisted in `~/.fuigo/trusted_folders.toml`) is honoured because the store is re-read per session.

**Murage asks the human instead (0.1.52, FUIGOTRUST1).** Murage keeps its own per-folder record (`folder-trust.json` in its data dir, keyed by canonical workspace root): a folder chosen in a working-folder picker on the desktop is trusted at selection time, folders bots were already working in before 0.1.52 are recorded once at the first boot (`seededFrom`; Forget in the picker asks again), and any other folder with trust-sensitive sources raises one "Trust this folder?" card before the engine starts — never auto-answered, never in Auto mode on its own, answerable only from an owner surface. Only when the person trusted the folder does Murage pass `--trust` (a top-level flag, before `agent`); "Don't trust" spawns without it and the conversation shows which sources were left out. Murage also advertises `fuigo/folderTrust.interactive` and answers Fuigo's `_fuigo/folder_trust/request` from the same decision. The decision is taken before the spawn on purpose: the engine reads project instructions and skills when it builds the session, so a grant given through the interactive request alone would reach `AGENTS.md` only on the next turn. `FUIGO_FOLDER_TRUST` is never set and the user's own Fuigo configuration (`~/.fuigo/config.toml`) is never rewritten (a provider-routed turn writes its own `config.toml` into a temporary home Murage owns, below). What happens to Fuigo's own trust store depends on which path the turn runs on:

- **Native-login turn** (the user's real `FUIGO_HOME`, else `~/.fuigo`): `--trust` is a Fuigo grant, so Fuigo itself persists the folder into the user's `trusted_folders.toml`, exactly as `fuigo --trust` in a terminal would; that is the one write Murage causes there, and only on a turn the person trusted. The reverse also holds: Fuigo's `decide` answers Trusted from that store before it ever asks, so a folder the person trusted in standalone Fuigo runs trusted in Murage whatever Murage's own record says. Murage reads the same file (read-only, same `FUIGO_HOME` resolution, the upstream longest-prefix/same-git-root cascade) and, for such a folder, raises no card, records nothing new and shows no "untrusted folder" chip — the picker says "Trusted by your own Fuigo install". A "Don't trust" in Murage cannot withhold a folder the user's own Fuigo trusts; forgetting it is `fuigo`'s job (edit or delete the entry in `trusted_folders.toml`).
- **Provider-routed turn** (a provider connection chosen in Murage): the engine runs under a per-turn temporary `FUIGO_HOME` under `<data dir>/native/provider-turns/`, created before the trust decision and removed when the turn ends (child close, a card that times out or is stopped, a launch that fails). That home has no `trusted_folders.toml`, so the user's standalone grants do not apply there, `--trust` persists only into the temporary home (discarded with it), and Murage's record is the only thing that speaks for the folder. Standalone Fuigo learns nothing from a routed turn.


Two auto-approve holes are closed on the engine side: `auto` mode no longer runs discarding `git checkout`/`git switch`/`git stash` forms (`git checkout -- file`, `git switch --discard-changes`, `git stash drop`) without consulting the classifier, and `rg --hostname-bin` no longer rides the safe-command allowlist; whatever the engine does not auto-approve arrives at Murage as an ordinary `session/request_permission` prompt. The remaining changes are engine-internal (subagents and workflow children inherit the parent's resolved `[toolset.bash]` parameters, an explicit `api_backend` survives a same-slug catalog sibling, a credential-less 401 whose auth recovery fails transiently parks the turn on the uncharged resubmit path instead of failing it, and a workflow resume refuses an unknown-outcome replay) and need no Murage driver change. `--no-memory`, `--no-leader`, `--permission-mode` and the `_fuigo/ask_user_question` shape Murage renders as a question card are unchanged.
